findings.title: KeyError on spans missing end_timestamp_precise
findings.body: The new code uses `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with subscript access, while every other optional field in the same Span constructor (parent_span_id, is_remote) uses `.get()`. Any span payload already buffered in the ingest-spans Kafka topic (or coming from a producer that has not yet been upgraded) that lacks this key will raise KeyError and crash the consumer batch. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise")` (or fall back to a sentinel such as 0.0) for forward compatibility with in-flight messages.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative slicing will raise AssertionError
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative integer) when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing; `QuerySet.__getitem__` asserts `int(k.start) >= 0` and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Any admin-supplied cursor string like `"0:-10:0"` (Cursor.from_string parses the second token via `int(bits[1])`) will crash the endpoint with a 500. This also contradicts the docstring claim that the feature is "safe" — it is not even reachable without a server error. Either remove the negative-offset branch or fetch a count first and translate the offset to a positive LIMIT/OFFSET in SQL.

findings.title: max_segment_spans protection silently removed from flush path
findings.body: `_load_segment_data` previously guarded against runaway segments by deleting any key whose accumulated span count exceeded `self.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and emitting the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. The diff deletes that branch entirely and the constructor parameter `max_segment_spans` is now dead — no code reads it. The new in-Lua `zpopmin` eviction runs on the insert path, but it does not protect against (a) segments populated before this rollout, (b) sets that exceed 1000 entries between two insert calls, or (c) the case where `zcard(set_key)` after `zunionstore` returns 0 because both source sets were empty (so eviction is skipped even though `zcard` afterward would still report >1000). Without the flush-time guard a single oversized segment will now be loaded into memory and serialized, which is exactly what the old check prevented.

findings.title: zpopmin eviction key is not actually oldest spans
findings.body: Eviction uses `zpopmin` against `end_timestamp_precise` scores. When many spans in a segment share the same `end_timestamp_precise` (which is the common case for spans belonging to the same transaction), Redis sorted-set ordering for ties is lexicographic on the member bytes, i.e. on the JSON payload. The "evict oldest" policy therefore degenerates to "evict whichever serialized payload sorts first," which is essentially arbitrary and may preferentially drop small/different payloads. The score should include a deterministic tiebreaker (e.g. span_id) so eviction order is reproducible.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator added with no test coverage
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-copy of BasePaginator.get_result with a security-relevant behavior change (allowing negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features=True`). It is wired into the audit-logs endpoint and gated only by `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but there are zero tests for the class itself, for `enable_advanced_features=True` path, for negative offsets, or for the auditlog endpoint's new `optimized_pagination=true` branch. A paginator that silently changes the cursor contract for admins deserves its own tests in tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py and tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py.

findings.title: Pre-existing typo order_b still present in BasePaginator.build_queryset
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.build_queryset` the branch that flips `-key` ordering back to ascending writes `queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by)` — `order_b` is not an attribute of `Query` (the correct attribute is `order_by`). As a result, the reversed ordering is silently dropped and the queryset is left ordered by `-key` even though the code intended `+key`. This is in the same file the diff touches and is exercised by every caller using a descending order_by with a `is_prev=True` cursor that has a cursor value. It must be fixed before this PR lands; the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` inherits from `BasePaginator` and inherits the bug.

findings.title: Endpoint change misrepresented as performance optimization
findings.body: The endpoint change is labeled "Performance optimization for high-volume audit log access patterns" and the new query parameter is named `optimized_pagination`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` produces the same SQL plan as `DateTimePaginator` for the normal (forward, non-negative offset) case; the only functional difference is that it permits negative cursor offsets. There is no benchmark, no documentation in `api-docs/` (Sentry typically gates new query params), and no mention that the new branch is only active for superusers/org members with global access — `enable_advanced_features=True` is silently enabled based on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, which is not the same permission check used elsewhere in this endpoint (`OrganizationAuditPermission`). Either rename the parameter to reflect what it actually does (e.g. `allow_negative_offset`) and document it, or drop the class.
